channel.title: The San Francisco Standard - Article Feed
channel.description: Latest articles from The San Francisco Standard (sfstandard.com)

item.title: With coaches and teachers on strike, SF students take matters into their own hands
item.description: Athletes are practicing and theater kids are rehearsing without faculty supervision.

item.title: Buster Posey is done shopping and ready to embrace competitions at Giants camp
item.description: Tony Vitello’s team needs young players to step into prominent roles, including Bryce Eldridge, who spent time shagging in the outfield Wednesday.

item.title: Inside the allegations against a San Francisco social climber accused of sex crimes
item.description: Mickey Gerold led a seemingly charmed life of private clubs and powerful friends. But behind closed doors, his ex claims, he coerced her into sex work.

item.title: SFUSD is losing millions during the strike. Are its homework packets a ploy for cash?
item.description: The United Educators of San Francisco suspect the independent study materials are a scheme to get state funding while schools are closed. The state says it won’t work.

item.title: As Macklin Celebrini takes the Olympic ice, Steph Curry is ready to tune in
item.description: The Golden State superstar isn’t the only fan of the Sharks phenom at 1 Warriors Way.

item.title: Newsom is MIA in schools shutdown. Plus: Where do SF electeds send their kids?
item.description: Also in today’s Power Play: A new Lurie-linked PAC emerges.

item.title: This downtown SF university gave up its campus. Here’s how it plans to rebuild
item.description: Golden Gate University President Brent White talks about the school’s “new direction.”

item.title: The sold-out Lunar New Year feast everyone wanted in on
item.description: Chef James Yeun Leong Parry of The Happy Crane joined forces with Sun Moon Studio’s Alan Hsu and Sarah Cooper for a one-night-only collaboration dinner.

item.title: The SFUSD teachers strike has now followed Maria Su home
item.description: Increasingly personal attacks on the superintendent have culminated in picketing outside of her house.

item.title: PG&E CEO recants claim that Lurie requested power to opera house during blackout
item.description: At a hearing on December’s PG&E blackout, CEO Sumeet Singh said Lurie pushed for power at the venue, a sensitive claim as the mayor’s daughter was performing there.
